reference: Kramida 2024, NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12), https://doi.org/10.18434/T4W30F
authors: A. Kramida, Yu. Ralchenko, J. Reader, and NIST ASD Team
title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12)
method: NIST critically evaluated compilation (see asd_compilation and asd_references for the original measurements)
uncertainty: per-level ASD uncertainties in column 'Uncertainty (cm-1)' (empty where ASD gives none)
conversion: Energies from 'ground state 2p6.3s 2S 1/2', energy zero: The ASD output and the downloaded bibliography pages do not state a hyperfine reference (levels are not hyperfine resolved). The adopted ionization energy (Ciocca 1992) applies to the mean of the 3S hyperfine levels.
caveats: Energies are term energies in cm^-1 relative to the ASD ground state 2p6.3s 2S 1/2; the ionization limit is a separate 'Limit' row and in ionization_energy.

ASD levels are not isotope resolved: the compilation mixes data from different isotopes and natural samples; isotope shifts and hyperfine structure are not separated. RydState 'Na' uses mass number 23; hyperfine structure is not resolved in ASD (centroid / fine-structure energies).
Energy precision is ASD's (compilation) precision; for many Rydberg series more precise modern measurements exist (e.g. mm-wave or laser spectroscopy) and should be preferred in fits.

Column j in levels.csv is the total J of the level as given by ASD; s is the total spin from the LS term multiplicity; for jj/jK-coupled terms only n and l are assigned. n, l are filled only when the configuration has exactly one electron outside the RydState core configuration '2p6' (same rule as rydstate.species.nist.parse_nist_energy_levels).
